$comment: The expo-updates fingerprints of the binaries currently in users' hands.
An `eas update` only reaches a build whose fingerprint matches exactly;
publishing to any other value reports success and reaches zero devices,
with no error anywhere. scripts/verify-ota-target.mjs compares the working
tree against this file and refuses to publish on a mismatch.
Update this file in the same commit that ships a new binary, and never to
silence the preflight — a mismatch means the update cannot land, not that
"setAside" lists files that landed on main after that binary was built and
only touch another platform's native code. scripts/publish-ota.mjs removes
them from its throwaway tree before fingerprinting that platform, so JS from
main still reaches the binary. Drop the list when that platform ships a new
binary. This file is not a fingerprint input, so editing it never moves one.

android.$note: Built from main e0f28361 (#212; EAS build e23bae27, workflow run 36109403959), submitted to the Play closed alpha 2026-09-25 (EAS submission c1185002) and promoted to production the same day (full rollout; Google published it at 09:44 UTC; managed publishing is off). It drops react-native-url-polyfill and its dependencies (#212), and it is the first binary to embed #205's trimmed fonts, which Play measured as 3.5 MB off a new install. The fingerprint equals a clean npm ci of e0f28361, computed before the build. Now the binary in every Play user's hands, so an update published against this fingerprint reaches production; 0.1.6 (74) at caae1cc09c42590610679de5bfd8a035f2bf9021 is only whatever has not updated yet.

ios.$note: Built from main e0f28361 (#212; EAS build dbcdbb19, workflow run 36109403959) and uploaded to TestFlight for the internal group 2026-09-25. It carries everything 0.1.6 (55 and 56) did, including the AI data-sharing consent (#209), and drops react-native-url-polyfill (#212). The fingerprint equals a clean npm ci of e0f28361, computed before the build. Submitted to App Review as version 0.1.7 on 2026-09-25 in place of 0.1.6 (56), and waiting for review again after a resubmission on 2026-09-26 (automatic release on approval). Hold iOS updates while it is in review, so the reviewer sees the build as submitted. Until Apple approves it, the App Store still serves 0.1.5 (54) at 835877cfddddf3644cf2e03bc8da01d7aec206d0, which no update from main can reach, so an update published against this fingerprint reaches TestFlight only.
